- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for 1–3 day horizons.
- After sharp price spikes (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; apply a 2–5% downward correction to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment shows strong negative momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative sentiment changes), model underestimates downside risk; add 1–2% buffer to forecast for 3–7 day horizons.
- When sentiment is neutral or volatile (±0.33), model exhibits mean-reversion bias; align forecast with 3–5 day moving average of historical prices.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently underestimates upward moves in high-news environments; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% if news volume > 3.0 and sentiment > 0.67.
- If sentiment turns bullish after a downtrend (e.g., negative → positive), model lags; add 1–2 day lag correction to forecast for 7–14 day horizons.
